what: Trump tells US negotiators 'not to rush' into deal with Iran

clean_source_blocks.text: The deal under discussion would involve a 60-day ceasefire extension during which the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened, according to US media.

US President Donald Trump has instructed his negotiators "not to rush into a deal" with Iran, after reports suggested an agreement was close. According to US media reports, the deal under discussion involves a 60-day ceasefire extension, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and further negotiations over Iran's nuclear programme. In a social media post, Trump said "constructive" talks were proceeding but "both sides must take their time and get it right". Trump said on Saturday an agreement had been "largely negotiated", prompting speculation an announcement could be imminent. But reports in Iranian media say there are still "one or two" points of disagreement in the potential deal. Iranian officials had also signalled progress in talks over the weekend, but foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said that did not mean agreements would be reached on key issues.

by ANISSA REYES | The National News Desk (TNND) — The United States is close to reaching a deal with Iran that could end the war, according to regional officials speaking to the Associated Press on Sunday. The deal would reopen the highly contended Strait of Hormuz and see Iran forfeiting its stockpile of highly enriched uranium. Details and timelines on the potential deal will be worked out later, according to the officials. Iran has not publicly committed to giving up its uranium, which has been a key demand of President Donald Trump. On Saturday, Trump revealed that a deal had been “largely negotiated,” after ongoing calls with Israel and other regional allies.

The US and its allies suspect that Iran is seeking to develop a nuclear weapon by enriching uranium - but Tehran has said its nuclear programme is solely for peaceful purposes. In his social media post, the US president also said Washington's blockade of Iranian ports - which has been in place since early April - will remain "in full force and effect until an agreement is reached, certified, and signed". The US has been enforcing its blockade to exert pressure on Tehran to agree to its terms. For its part, Iran has continued to control the Strait of Hormuz, effectively closing the vital waterway through which around 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas travels. The move has sent oil prices soaring globally.

[Lähde: BBC World]
US President Donald Trump has instructed his negotiators "not to rush into a deal" with Iran, after reports suggested an agreement was close.

According to US media reports, the deal under discussion involves a 60-day ceasefire extension, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and further negotiations over Iran's nuclear programme.

In a social media post, Trump said "constructive" talks were proceeding but "both sides must take their time and get it right".

Trump said on Saturday an agreement had been "largely negotiated", prompting speculation an announcement could be imminent.

But reports in Iranian media say there are still "one or two" points of disagreement in the potential deal.

Iranian officials had also signalled progress in talks over the weekend, but foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said that did not mean agreements would be reached on key issues.

Israel and the US launched massive air strikes on Iran on 28 February. Tehran retaliated by firing drones and missiles at Israel and US targets in countries across the Gulf.

A ceasefire agreed in April meant to facilitate talks has largely been observed, despite occasional exchanges of fire.

In Sunday's post on Truth Social, Trump said negotiations "are proceeding in an orderly and constructive manner, and I have informed my representatives not to rush into a deal in that time is on our side".

"Both sides must take their time and get it right. There can be no mistakes!"

Trump also said Iran "must understand" it cannot develop a nuclear weapon, a stance he has frequently reiterated and that is shared by Israel and other Western allies.

The US and its allies suspect that Iran is seeking to develop a nuclear weapon by enriching uranium - but Tehran has said its nuclear programme is solely for peaceful purposes.

In his social media post, the US president also said Washington's blockade of Iranian ports - which has been in place since early April - will remain "in full force and effect until an agreement is reached, certified, and signed".

The US has been enforcing its blockade to exert pressure on Tehran to agree to its terms.

For its part, Iran has continued to control the Strait of Hormuz, effectively closing the vital waterway through which around 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas travels. The move has sent oil prices soaring globally.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio earlier said that "significant" but "not final" progress had been made in the negotiations.

[Lähde: WXLV ABC 45]
by ANISSA REYES | The National News Desk

(TNND) — The United States is close to reaching a deal with Iran that could end the war, according to regional officials speaking to the Associated Press on Sunday.

The deal would reopen the highly contended Strait of Hormuz and see Iran forfeiting its stockpile of highly enriched uranium.

Details and timelines on the potential deal will be worked out later, according to the officials.

Iran has not publicly committed to giving up its uranium, which has been a key demand of President Donald Trump. On Saturday, Trump revealed that a deal had been “largely negotiated,” after ongoing calls with Israel and other regional allies.

On a visit to India, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, said that “significant profress, although not final progress, has been made,” regarding negotiations, and that the world did not need to fear Iran having a nuclear weapon.

Meanwhile Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian told state TV that they were ready “to assure the world that we are not after a nuclear weapon.” However, the embassy of Iran in India responded to Rubio on social media, saying Tehran has an “inalienable” right to nuclear technology.

Iran has repeatedly insisted that its nuclear program is peaceful while enriching uranium to near weapons-grade levels.

payload.title: Trump kehottaa Yhdysvaltain neuvottelijoita olemaan kiirehtimättä Iran-sopimusta
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump on kehottanut neuvottelijoitaan etenemään varovasti Iranin kanssa käytävissä neuvotteluissa, vaikka sopimuksen on raportoitu olevan lähellä.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump on kehottanut maan neuvottelijoita olemaan kiirehtimättä sopimukseen Iranin kanssa sen jälkeen, kun yhdysvaltalaismediassa oli kerrottu mahdollisen järjestelyn olevan lähellä. Raporttien mukaan neuvoteltavana oleva sopimus voisi pidentää tulitaukoa 60 päivällä, avata Hormuzinsalmen uudelleen ja jatkaa keskusteluja Iranin ydinohjelmasta.

## Neuvottelujen sanotaan edenneen

Trump sanoi sosiaalisessa mediassa, että keskustelut ovat olleet rakentavia, mutta osapuolten on hänen mukaansa käytettävä aikaa ja varmistettava, että ratkaisu tehdään oikein. Hän oli aiemmin sanonut, että sopimus oli pitkälti neuvoteltu, mikä lisäsi odotuksia mahdollisesta nopeasta ilmoituksesta.

Iranilaismediassa on kuitenkin kerrottu, että mahdollisessa sopimuksessa on yhä yksi tai kaksi erimielisyyttä. Iranin ulkoministeriön tiedottaja Esmail Baghaei on viestinyt neuvotteluissa tapahtuneesta edistyksestä, mutta korostanut, ettei se tarkoita automaattisesti sitä, että keskeisistä kysymyksistä päästäisiin sopuun.

Yhdysvaltalaisraporttien mukaan esillä oleva järjestely voisi sisältää myös jatkoneuvotteluja Iranin ydinohjelmasta. Eräiden alueellisten viranomaisten mukaan sopimus voisi johtaa siihen, että Iran luopuisi korkeasti rikastetun uraanin varastoistaan. Iran ei kuitenkaan ole julkisesti sitoutunut tällaiseen ehtoon.

## Hormuzinsalmi on sopimuksen keskeinen osa

Hormuzinsalmen avaaminen olisi neuvottelujen merkittävimpiä kohtia. Iran on pitänyt salmea hallinnassaan ja käytännössä sulkenut tärkeän meriväylän, jonka kautta kulkee huomattava osa maailman öljystä ja nesteytetystä maakaasusta. Sulku on nostanut öljyn hintaa maailmanmarkkinoilla.

Yhdysvallat on puolestaan pitänyt voimassa Iranin satamiin kohdistuvaa saartoa, jonka kerrotaan alkaneen huhtikuun alussa. Trumpin mukaan saarto pysyy voimassa, kunnes sopimus on saavutettu, varmennettu ja allekirjoitettu.

Yhdysvallat ja sen liittolaiset epäilevät Iranin pyrkivän kehittämään ydinaseen rikastamalla uraania. Iran on kiistänyt väitteet ja sanoo ydinohjelmansa olevan yksinomaan rauhanomainen. Neuvottelujen eteneminen näyttää siksi riippuvan sekä turvallisuusjärjestelyistä että siitä, miten ydinohjelmaa koskevat vaatimukset kirjataan mahdolliseen sopimukseen.
